hero.kicker: Concept for a bug-bounty and vulnerability programme
hero.title: The exploited list, turned into a queue you can close.
hero.body: bountystash reads CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue, groups entries by the effort a fix actually takes, and writes the result as a work order: what is being exploited against your stack, in the order that removes the most risk per hour spent. No scanner noise. No thousand-page report. One queue with owners and a closing note.

stats.label: of sample exposure closed by three patches

kev.title: Sample queue
kev.note: Sample data. The CVE identifiers and products are real and well known; effort, exposure and ordering are invented to show the interface. Nothing here is a live programme.

clustersNote: The top three clusters of the sample queue. A cluster is a group of entries one team can close in one sitting, ordered by the exposure it removes, not by CVSS.

clusters.name: Remote access
clusters.action: Both are pre-authentication and both appear in ransomware chains. The edge device is the door; patch it first, then check for the webshell.

clusters.name: Edge appliances
clusters.action: One management-plane path, one protocol-level reset. The reset is a limit change on the load balancer; the other needs a maintenance window.

clusters.name: Java estates
clusters.action: Most of the effort is discovery: which jars are actually loaded, and which of them the application server unpacks into a directory it serves.

method.title: Intake
method.body: Two inputs: the catalogue, refreshed on every publish, and your asset list. Anything you cannot name an owner for is treated as exposed until proven otherwise.

method.title: Triage
method.body: Entries that cannot touch your stack are dropped with the reason written down, so the queue is short and every removal is auditable.

method.title: Reproduce
method.body: For the top of the queue, a proof in your own environment: the request, the response, and the line in the config that made it possible.

method.title: Close
method.body: Patch order, the verification that proves it took, and a one-page note your auditor can file. The entry leaves the queue only when the note exists.

programNote: Concept, not an offer. Each shape exists to answer one question a security budget always asks: what does a closed finding cost us?

tiers.name: Pilot
tiers.body: One product team, one queue ordered by effort, with proof for the top five entries and a patch plan the team can start on Monday.

tiers.name: Retainer
tiers.body: New catalogue entries mapped to owners as they publish, a closing report your auditors accept, and a quarterly review of what the queue says about your estate.

tiers.name: Incident
tiers.body: When something on the list lands on you: scoping, exposure check, the order to patch in, and the write-up the day after.

footer: bountystash — concept mockup by Matt Ji. Sample data, no live programme, no tracking. The real portfolio is bountystash.com.
